$comment: The source of sf-badge's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/badge (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

line.summary: Takes the text line of this form size, for a table cell or a row of fields, so the row keeps its control height.

appearance.summary: How the badge looks: the most visible fill, a calmer tonal one, or an outline.

scheme.summary: Which semantic colour the badge takes. A status word given here still works and reaches the status axis.

status.summary: What the badge reports, in the shared status vocabulary. The word this component used before, danger, is still accepted and means error.

relations.name: sr-only/default
$comment: The badge names itself through a visually hidden label; the utility comes
with the component rather than from a scan, which a badge inside another
component's markup can miss -- and then the label reads beside the text

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

accessibility.$comment: No role of its own: the badge is text. With aria-label the label is said through a visually hidden span and the visible text is hidden from assistive technology; with neither text nor aria-label the badge is decorative and aria-hidden.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-badge for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.note: stays a host attribute, read by the base (§3.1, §4.8); no shim
the legacy axis name; the shim maps the attribute and the property
rows.summary: Legacy name for appearance, still honoured. See contracts/public-api-axes.json.

rows.note: journal attribute-icon-left-right-to-start-end; icon-start wins when both are given
journal attribute-icon-left-right-to-start-end; icon-end wins when both are given
the physical name the template read as start
the physical name the template read as end

x-summary: A short non-interactive label for a status, category, version or count beside an object, drawn in a size, appearance and colour role or status. It adds no keyboard or pointer behaviour.
x-renamed: settings.aria-label: a host attribute, read by the base, never a setting (§3.1)
x-decisions: a11y-role: none -- the badge is text, drawn in a span; it takes no role. The name is the host's aria-label (said through a visually hidden span, the visible text then hidden from assistive technology), else its text or text slot; with neither, the badge is decorative and aria-hidden (§4.8).

legacy names: type -> appearance, icon-left -> icon-start and icon-right -> icon-end leave the settings and are dated setting aliases (aliases.json, until 2026-12-01; journal attribute-icon-left-right-to-start-end); the values danger -> error (status) and left/right -> start/end (icon-position) are dated value aliases.

scheme keeps routing a status word (info, success, warning, error, danger) to the status axis in code: scheme stays its own axis for the colour role (journal attribute-badge-scheme-to-status, public-api-axes legacy_input_remains_its_own_axis), which a setting alias, one name for another, cannot say.
icon-start and icon-end are optional (§4.2) and keep their own getters: an empty attribute («no icon here») suppresses the icon shortcut, an absent one lets it through.
aria-label is a host attribute, never a setting (§3.1); the template reads it from the host.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one (a copy nothing draws would drift).

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (Новый, primary; its type="fill" is not an appearance and reads as main) plus tonal and outline, the statuses, icons, a labelled count and the line sizes.
css-variables: the nine public variables of src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json the class sheet already reads (§6).

folder: badges takes the tag's name, badge (§3, §21, §16 item 16); the loader bundle is cl-badge, cl-badges is a Loader forward (src/core/contracts/smart-rule-forwards.v1.json) and smart/badges/js/badges.js a forwarding script until 2026-12-01 (change journal path-smart-badges-to-badge). The registry id follows the folder: smart.badge (smart.badges is its dated alias in the same record).
version 1.1.0: renamed members behind dated aliases are a minor (§4.10, §16.20).

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.1.2: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

$comment-after: The bundle's former name cl-badges (the folder was `badges` until standard
1.3.8 §3, §21 gave it the tag's name) is not a rule here: a rule of type
smart is a Smart component to the registry, and this one has no element. The
Loader forwards it to cl-badge from src/core/contracts/

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-badge for a short non-interactive status, category, version or count beside an object.
do_not: Do not use Badge as a button, filter chip or notification
Do not communicate status by colour alone
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

accessibility.focus: Badge is static metadata and does not enter the tab order.
